newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Spitaels to face Dassault probe police.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Spitaels to face Dassault probe police.

text.p: Belgian socialist party figurehead Guy Spitaels is set to be questioned by police over allegations his party accepted bribes from French plane maker Dassault after a regional assembly was recommended to lift his parliamentary immunity.

The Walloon Parliament is due to vote on the proposal on Wednesday, but the outcome is not in doubt after an all-party committee unanimously recommended in the early hours of Tuesday morning that Spitaels should temporarily lose his protective privilege.
Spitaels, who has denied all knowledge of the allegations made against him, has said he is willing to help the police.

Spitaels was President of Belgium's French-speaking Socialist Party (PS) in the late 1980s when it is alleged Dassault paid millions of francs in bribes to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to the country's F-16 fighter jets.

Two Socialist Party officials were charged last week with corruption. Their lawyers have said they received 30 million francs (about $1 million) on behalf of the PS from Dassault, but Dassault has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

One of the men arrested implicated Spitaels and also said present PS President Philippe Busquin knew of the affair, sparking calls from opposition groups that the PS should pull out of Belgium's government. The PS is one of four parties making up the coalition.

It was not immediately clear if Spitaels would have to resign his present post of President of the Walloon Parliament, the regional assembly serving Belgium's southern French-speaking areas. The lifting of immunity will be limited until June 30, 1997.
Some members of the parliament have suggested he takes a "holiday" until the affair is over.
